sources.rrtmg: AER RRTMG_LW and RRTMG_SW standard-atmosphere examples (github.com/AER-RC/RRTMG_LW and RRTMG_SW, run_examples_std_atm: input_rrtm_<ATM>-clr and output_rrtm_<ATM>-clr, clear sky); RRTMG is within 1.5 W/m2 of LBLRTM in clear-sky longwave flux (Iacono et al. 2008, JGR 113, D13103). Longwave 10-3250 cm-1, black surface; shortwave 820-50000 cm-1, solar constant 1360.85 W/m2, surface albedo 0.2, Rayleigh scattering, no aerosol
sources.afgl: AFGL atmospheric constituent profiles (Anderson et al. 1986, AFGL-TR-86-0110) as distributed with libRadtran (data/atmmod/afgl*.dat), H2O and O3 as dry volume mixing ratios
sources.iae: Feigelson et al. 1991, JGR 96, 8985, Table 6: ICRCCM line-by-line (IAE) fluxes for the McClatchey profiles, H2O with continuum, CO2 300 ppmv, O3, 0-2600 cm-1
sources.mlawer: Mlawer et al. 1997, JGR 102, 16663: Table 5 (LBLRTM MLS, CO2 355 ppmv, CKD_2.0) and Table 6 (doubling CO2 355 -> 710 ppmv, MLS, by band)
sources.iacono: Iacono et al. 2008, JGR 113, D13103, Tables 2 and 3: LBLRTM and CHARTS forcings on the MLS profile (RTMIP cases of Collins et al. 2006)
sources.chou: Chou et al. 2001, NASA TM-2001-104606 vol. 19, Tables 14-15 (line-by-line longwave by band, MLS and SAW, CO2 350 ppmv, no minor gases) and Table 16 (the minor gases' effects on the fluxes as computed by their parameterization, not line-by-line: CH4 1.75, N2O 0.28 ppmv, CFCs and the minor CO2 bands); Chou and Suarez 1999, NASA TM-1999-104606 vol. 15, Tables 7-8 (line-by-line shortwave, MLS, solar zenith angle 60 degrees, CO2 350 ppmv)

iae.note: surface up, surface down, OLR at 100 km; CO2 300 ppmv, no CH4/N2O

doubling.note: CO2 355 -> 710 ppmv, reduction of net upward flux at TOA and tropopause, increase of downward flux at the surface

co2Doubling.note: MLS, CO2 287 -> 574 ppmv, CH4 806 ppbv, N2O 275 ppbv; LBLRTM longwave and CHARTS shortwave forcing (decrease of net upward longwave, increase of net downward shortwave)

vapour120.note: MLS at 574 ppmv CO2, H2O x1.2 in every layer

chouLongwave.note: line-by-line, CO2 350 ppmv, no minor gases, stratospheric q 4e-6 g/g; [band from, to, surface down, TOA up]

chouShortwave.note: MLS, solar zenith angle 60 degrees, CO2 350 ppmv; table 7 surface albedo 0, change of surface downward flux with each absorber (overlap with H2O included); table 8 surface albedo 0.2, no scattering, net downward at TOA and surface and absorbed in the atmosphere

wild2019.note: global annual clear-sky means of Wild et al. 2019 (Clim. Dyn.); the OLR range is CERES EBAF clear-sky
